chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: That a man who was in Hamadan narrated that his father died and was not familiar with this matter, and he made a will at the time of death, instructing that something be given in the way of Allah.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how should it be done? And we informed him that he was not familiar with this matter, so he said: 'If a man had instructed me to place [it] with a Jew or a Christian, I would have placed it with them.'
Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is upon those who alter it.'
So look to whoever goes out to this direction, meaning the frontiers (Thughur), and send it to him.'
ai.seo_question: How should a vague or unknown bequest in a will be executed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the case of a deceased person in Hamadan who bequeathed to 'the way of Allah' but was unfamiliar with the specific theological meaning of the term. Citing Surah al-Baqarah 2:181 regarding the alteration of wills, the Imam argues that since the testator's intent was ambiguous, the executor has the discretion to interpret 'the way of Allah' as jihad in the frontiers (Thughur), thereby ensuring the bequest serves a concrete religious purpose rather than remaining undefined.
